concepts.label: vertex
concepts.gloss: A vertex is a node in the topology that functions as a forwarding realm and can host spans within a larger fabric.

concepts.label: span-cap-point
concepts.gloss: A span-cap-point is a termination point located on a vertex that marks where a span begins and ends, and terminates the corresponding span.

concepts.label: shifting-span
concepts.gloss: A shifting-span is an adaptation that bridges a span by shifting its position at a vertex and adapts another component within the topology.

concepts.label: offer-gateway-point
concepts.gloss: An offer-gateway-point is an access point on a vertex that provides access to a carriage-offer service.

concepts.label: carriage-offer
concepts.gloss: A carriage-offer is a service offering that uses an access point and is realized by a circuit-end-point across a span within the fabric.

concepts.label: tier-stream-qualifier
concepts.gloss: A tier-stream-qualifier is a multiplex that maps or qualifies a service tier into a stream, thereby linking to an offer.

concepts.label: vertex-gate-set
concepts.gloss: A vertex-gate-set is a switching construct on a vertex that holds gates enabling path switching.

concepts.label: span
concepts.gloss: A span is a link connecting two vertices, terminated by a span-cap-point.

concepts.label: fabric
concepts.gloss: A fabric is a topology that contains the vertices and spans, representing the overall forwarding realm.

concepts.label: circuit-end-point
concepts.gloss: A circuit-end-point is an endpoint associated with a vertex that is part of a carriage-offer service.
